title: Headache
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with bilateral, pressing/tightening (non-pulsating), mild to moderate intensity headache without nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or phonophobia. No aura. Not aggravated by routine physical activity. Duration 30 min to 7 days. Tension headache is the most common primary headache disorder — bilateral, band-like pressure. Distinguish from migraine (unilateral, pulsating, moderate-severe, nausea/photophobia, aggravated by activity) and cluster (unilateral with autonomic features). No imaging needed if history/neuro exam normal. Treatment: acute — NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or acetaminophen. Avoid opioid and butalbital-containing analgesics (rebound headache risk). Prophylaxis if frequent: amitriptyline, nortriptyline (TCAs first-line). Non-pharmacologic: stress management, trigger avoidance, relaxation techniques, biofeedback.
